name: Mangulam
info: Home to the earliest dated Tamil-Brahmi rock-cut inscriptions (circa 3rd–2nd century BCE). The inscriptions explicitly record gifts and rock beds gifted to Jain monks by the Early Pandya ruler Nedunchezhiyan.

name: Thirupparankundram
info: Features 2nd century BCE Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions carved into the rock cavern beds. Notably records donations made by a householder from ancient Sri Lanka (Eelak-kudumpikan), demonstrating early trans-oceanic cultural links.

name: Samanarmalai
info: A renowned hill complex in Keelakuyilkudi featuring ancient Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions, Vatteluttu records, carved rock-cut beds, and remarkable bas-relief sculptures of Jain Tirthankaras dating from the 3rd century BCE to the 10th century CE.

name: Arittapatti
info: Recognized as a biological and historical heritage site. The granitic hillocks shelter 2,200-year-old Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions and sculpted drip ledges chiseled for ascetic monks meditating in rock shelters.

name: Sittanavasal
info: Celebrated for the rock-cut cave temple Arivar Koil and the 'Ezhadippattam' cavern. Contains 2nd century BCE Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions identifying the names of ascetic monks alongside famous 7th-century Jain fresco murals.

name: Jambai
info: Site of the momentous 1st-century CE Tamil-Brahmi inscription carved on a rock cave. It bears the title 'Satyaputo' given to the chieftain Adiyaman Neduman Anji, corroborating Sangam poetry and Ashokan edicts.

name: Pugalur
info: Located on the Pugalur Malai near the Cauvery River. Features six 1st–2nd century CE Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions recording three generations of Chera kings of the Irumporai lineage donating rock shelters to Jain ascetics.

name: Keezhadi
info: A major Sangam-era urban settlement excavated along the Vaigai river basin, dated scientifically to the 6th century BCE. Hundreds of potsherds bearing Tamil-Brahmi script names push back the antiquity of Tamil literacy.

name: Kodumanal
info: An ancient industrial and quartz-bead manufacturing trade center on the Noyyal river, celebrated in Sangam literature. Excavations uncovered hundreds of inscribed Tamil-Brahmi potsherds and megalithic cist burials.

name: Porunthal
info: An extensive Megalithic burial site near Palani. Excavations yielded intact ring-stands and pots inscribed in Tamil-Brahmi containing well-preserved paddy grains carbon-dated to circa 490 BCE.
